steps.narr: The filleted plate. We will machine it from aluminium bar on a small 3018 router.

steps.text: Make a CAM program on the Generic 3018 in aluminium: face the stock, adaptive-rough around the boss with the 6 mm endmill, open the bore with the 3 mm, pilot-drill the mounting holes, then cut the outline through with 4 tabs. Stock = bbox + 3 mm, 1 mm extra on top.
steps.narr: Describe the job the way you would brief a machinist: machine, material, stock, and the operations in order.

steps.name: cam_context
steps.result: Machines: Generic 3018 (300×180×45, 1000–10000 rpm)… Tools: T1 6 mm flat, T2 3 mm flat, T5 3 mm drill… Vertical round holes (5): Ø5 ×4 through, Ø8 through
steps.narr: cam_context gives the agent your machine and tool libraries plus facts about the model, including the holes it found from the B-rep.

steps.text: Aluminium on a 3018 is spindle-limited (10,000 rpm), so I'll take feeds from the calculator (6 mm: 1020 mm/min at S10000, 3 mm: 410 mm/min) and keep the adaptive stepover at 15 % so the 6 mm cutter can run full depth.
steps.narr: Feeds and speeds come from a calculator (13 materials, clamped to the machine's spindle and feed limits), not from memory.

steps.name: build_cam
steps.code:
part = bodies["Plate"]
stock = Stock.from_model(part, margin=3, top=1.0)
setup = Setup(machines["Generic 3018"], stock, origin="stock-top-left")
t6, t3, drl = (apply_feeds(tools[n], "aluminium", setup.machine) for n in (1, 2, 5))
mount = [h for h in holes(part) if h.diameter < 6]
program = Program(setup, name="plate")
program.add(face(setup, t6, z_top=stock.top, z_bottom=19))
program.add(adaptive(setup, t6, stock_minus(setup, part, 0.0, expand=6), z_top=19, z_bottom=4, stepover=0.15, stock_to_leave=0.3, name="Rough around boss"))
program.add(adaptive(setup, t3, circle(0, 0, 8), z_top=19, z_bottom=-4.5, stepover=0.15, name="Bore"))
program.add(drill(setup, drl, mount, peck="auto", name="Mounting holes (pilot)"))
program.add(contour(setup, t6, section(part, 0.0), z_top=4, z_bottom=-4.5, tabs=4, name="Outline"))
steps.result: Program 'plate' on Generic 3018 (grbl): 5 ops, est. 23.4 min
steps.narr: CAM is a second script, cam.py, saved next to the design. Each line is one operation on geometry taken straight from the exact model: section, holes, stock_minus.

Toolpaths draw over the model: rapids red, each operation its own colour, the stock as a yellow box. The orange spiral is the adaptive op: the tool never exceeds its target engagement, so it can cut full flute depth.

The head of the exported file: the warnings, units and WCS, then the first tool. G2/G3 appear where the path is circular.

steps.text: Exported **plate.nc**. Two things to check before you run it: toolpath goes 1.40 mm below the stock bottom (into the spoilboard?); Rough around boss: adaptive: engagement rises to 170° in corners (target 46°); feed is reduced there. The Ø5 holes are only piloted at Ø3 — say the word and I'll add a 3 mm helical bore to open them to size.
steps.narr: The agent passes the post's warnings on instead of hiding them. That is the end of the series; the docs cover every tool and setting in depth.
